## Proof

Let $M$ be a closed, connected, oriented $n$-manifold, so that the fundamental class $[M] \in H_n(M,\mathbb{Z})$ is defined and generates $H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}$.

We claim that the image $i([M]) \in H_n(M,\mathbb{C})$ under the coefficient map $i\colon H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \to H_n(M,\mathbb{C})$ is a fundamental class with $\mathbb{C}$-coefficients, i.e., it generates $H_n(M,\mathbb{C})$ as a $\mathbb{C}$-module.

**Step 1: Compute $H_n(M,\mathbb{C})$ via the Universal Coefficient Theorem.**

The universal coefficient theorem for homology gives a short exact sequence
$$0 \to H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \otimes \mathbb{C} \to H_n(M,\mathbb{C}) \to \mathrm{Tor}(H_{n-1}(M,\mathbb{Z}),\, \mathbb{C}) \to 0.$$

Since $\mathbb{C}$ (as an abelian group) is torsion-free and divisible, $\mathrm{Tor}(A, \mathbb{C}) = 0$ for every abelian group $A$. Hence the Tor term vanishes, and
$$H_n(M,\mathbb{C}) \cong H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \otimes \mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{Z} \otimes \mathbb{C} \cong \mathbb{C}.$$

**Step 2: Identify the coefficient map under this isomorphism.**

Under the UCT isomorphism $H_n(M,\mathbb{C}) \cong H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \otimes \mathbb{C}$, the coefficient map $i\colon H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \to H_n(M,\mathbb{C})$ corresponds to the natural map
$$H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \to H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \otimes \mathbb{C}, \qquad \alpha \mapsto \alpha \otimes 1.$$

(This is the standard description: the injection in the UCT short exact sequence is exactly the tensor map $\alpha \mapsto \alpha \otimes 1$.)

**Step 3: Show $i([M])$ generates $H_n(M,\mathbb{C})$.**

Since $[M]$ generates $H_n(M,\mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}$, every element of $H_n(M,\mathbb{Z})$ is $k[M]$ for some $k \in \mathbb{Z}$. Under the isomorphism $\mathbb{Z} \otimes \mathbb{C} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathbb{C}$, $k[M] \otimes 1$ maps to $k \cdot 1_{\mathbb{C}}$. In particular,
$$i([M]) \;\longleftrightarrow\; [M] \otimes 1 \;\longleftrightarrow\; 1 \in \mathbb{C}.$$

Since $1$ generates $\mathbb{C}$ as a $\mathbb{C}$-module (it is a basis vector of the $1$-dimensional $\mathbb{C}$-vector space $\mathbb{C}$), $i([M])$ generates $H_n(M,\mathbb{C}) \cong \mathbb{C}$ as a $\mathbb{C}$-module.

**Conclusion.**

The image $i([M]) \in H_n(M,\mathbb{C})$ is a generator of $H_n(M,\mathbb{C}) \cong \mathbb{C}$, hence it is a fundamental class for $M$ with $\mathbb{C}$-coefficients. The key point is that $\mathbb{C}$ is torsion-free (so the Tor term in the UCT vanishes, making $i$ injective) and that $[M] \otimes 1$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-basis of $\mathbb{Z}\langle[M]\rangle \otimes \mathbb{C}$, so the image of the $\mathbb{Z}$-generator becomes a $\mathbb{C}$-generator.

### PROOF COMPLETE
